subject: social_science
chapter_title: The State, the Government, and You

concepts.title: The State and the Government
concepts.definition: The state is the permanent political community with its territory, people and institutions; the government is only its temporary crew, elected or appointed for a time to run the state's affairs.
concepts.formula: state = people + territory + institutions; government = the team in office
concepts.key_idea: Governments come and go, the state remains: criticising a party is not attacking the country.
question_patterns: what is the difference between a state and a government

concepts.title: The State's Rulebook: An RWA Example
concepts.definition: The chapter uses a Resident Welfare Association: its rulebook decides how the committee is elected, how funds are spent and how disputes are heard; a constitution plays the same role for the state.
concepts.key_idea: Small societies need written rules; a huge state cannot function without one supreme rulebook.

what happens when a committee ignores its rulebook

who follows the rulebook in an association

concepts.title: Levels of Government
concepts.definition: India's government works at three levels, the Union at the centre, states, and local bodies in villages and cities; each level has its own powers and all play different, complementary roles.
concepts.key_idea: A subcontinent-sized democracy divides its work: big questions to the centre, local drains to the local body.

concepts.title: Your Part in the State
concepts.definition: The state is not someone else: every citizen pays taxes, follows just laws, votes, questions wrongs and can serve; Socrates' warning that shirking rule leaves you ruled by worse men calls citizens to participate.
concepts.key_idea: Democracy hands the state to its citizens: stepping back is also a choice, with its own price.
